σῖτος.as:
σῖτος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for דָּגָן ;]
wheat, corn: Mt 3:1213:25, 29, 30Mk 4:28, Lk 3:1712:1816:722:31, Jo 12:24, Ac 27:38, I Co 15:37, Re 6:618:13.†

Σίμων.sd: Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites
Σίμων.as:
Σίμων, -ωνος, ὁ
a Greek name (transliterated סִימוֺן in Heb.) used as a substitute for Συμεών (q.v.), Simon
1.Simon Peter: Mt 17:25, Mk 1:29, al.
2.Simon the Zealot (v.s. ζηλωτής, Καναναῖος): Mt 10:4, Mk 3:18, Lk 6:15, Ac 1:13.
3. One of the Brethren of our Lord (v.s. ἀδελψός): Mt 13:55, Mk 6:3.
4. The father of Judas Iscariot, himself surnamed Ἰσκαριώτης (q.v.): Jo 6:7112:4 (Rec.) 13:2, 26
5.Simon the Cyrenian: Mt 27:32, Mk 15:21, Lk 23:26.
6.Simon the Pharisee: Lk 7:40, 43, 44.
7.Simon of Bethany, surnamed ὁ λεπρός: Mt 26:6, Mk 14:3.
8.Simon Magus, a Samaritan sorcerer: Ac 8:9, 13, 18, 24.
9.Simon the tanner, of Joppa: Ac 9:4310:6, 17, 32.

σιαγών.sd: the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face
σιαγών.as:
σιαγών, -όνος, ἡ
[in LXX for לְחִי ;]
the jawbone, jaw, cheek: Mt 5:39, Lk 6:29 (cf. MM, xxii).†

Σιδών.long: Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia.
Σιδών.sd: Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine
Σιδών.as:
Σιδών, -ῶνος, ἡ (Heb. צִידוֹן),
Sidon, a maritime city of Phœnicia: Mt 11:21, 2215:21, Mk 3:87:24, 31, Lk 6:1710:13, 14, Ac 27:3.†

σίναπι.long: mustard (probably the shrub, not the herb).
σίναπι.as:
† σίναπι, -εως, τό
(prob. Egyptian), = Attic τὸ νᾶπυ
mustard: Mt 13:3117:20, Mk 4:31, Lk 13:1917:6.†

σιωπάω.long: I keep silence, am silent, either voluntarily or involuntarily.
σιωπάω.sd: properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602 (σιγή), which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water)
σιωπάω.as:
σιωπάω, -ῶ
(< σιωπή, silence) [in LXX for חשׁה, חרשׁ hi., etc. ;]
to be silent or still, keep silence: Mt 20:3126:63, Mk 3:49:3410:4814:61, Lk 19:4 , Ac 18:9; of one dumb, Lk 1:20 (cf. IV Mac 10:18); addressed rhetorically to the sea, σιώπα, Mk 4:39.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιγάω (q.v.).

Σιών.long: Zion, the hill; used for Jerusalem or heaven.
Σιών.sd: Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant)
Σιών.as:
Σιών
indecl.,
in NT anarth., but in LXX when used of the city of Jerusalem, ἡ Σ.
(Heb. צִיּוֹן),
Zion;
1. the mountain: in typical sense, of the Church, He 12:22; of heaven, Re 14:1.
2. The city, i.e. Jerusalem; in poetical sense;
(a) of the inhabitants: θυγάτηρ Σ, Mt 21:5, Jo 12:15(LXX);
(b) in wider sense, of Israel: Ro 11:26;
(c) fig.: τίθήμι ἐν Σ λίθον, Ro 9:33, I Pe 2:6(LXX).†

σιτιστός.as:
**† σιτιστός, -ή, -όν
(< σιτίζω, to fatten) [in Sm.: Ps 21 (22):13, Je 46 (26):21 * ;]
= σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: Mt 22:4.†

σινδών.sd: byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it)
σινδών.as:
σινδών, -όνος, ἡ
[in LXX: Jg 14:12, 13A, Pr 31:24 (סָדִין), I Mac 10:64 A * ;]
fine linen cloth;
(a) as used for swathing dead bodies (cf. Hdt., ii, 86): Mt 27:59, Mk 15:46, Lk 23:53;
(b) a garment or wrap of this material (cf. ICC, Jg, l.c.): Mk 14:51, 52.†

σίκερα.sd: an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor
σίκερα.as:
† σίκερα, τό indecl.
(Aram. שִׁכְרָא), [in LXX for שֵׁכָר (also rendered μέθυσμα, Jg 13:4, Mi 2:11), Le 10:9, al. ;]
fermented liquor, strong drink: Lk 1:15.†

Σιδώνιος.sd: a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon
Σιδώνιος.as:
Σιδώνιος, -α, -ον
(< Σιδών),
of Sidon, Sidonian;
(a) the region: sc. χώρα, Lk 4:26;
(b) the people: Ac 12:20.†

σιγάω.long: intrans: I am silent, keep silence; trans: I keep secret; pass: I am kept secret.
σιγάω.as:
σιγάω, -ῶ
(< σιγή), [in LXX for חרשׁ, חשׁה, etc. ;]
1. intrans., to be silent, keep silence: Lk 9:3618:3920:26, Ac 12:1715:12, 13, I Co 14:28, 30, 34.
2. Trans., to keep secret; pass., to be kept secret: Ro 16:25.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιωπάω

σιτομέτριον.g: a measured portion of grain or food
σιτομέτριον.long: a measured portion of grain or food.
σιτομέτριον.sd: a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food)
σιτομέτριον.as:
*† σιτομέτριον, -ου, τό
(< σιτομετρέω, Ge 47:12, 14 *, = Attic τὸν σῖτον μετρέω),
a measured portion of food: Lk 12:42 (for exx. in π., v. Deiss., BS, 158; LAE, 1031).†

Σιλωάμ.long: Siloam, a spring within the walls, in the south-east corner of Jerusalem.
Σιλωάμ.sd: Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem
Σιλωάμ.as:
Σιλωάμ (indecl., but in FlJ, gen., ᾶ, B.J., ii, 16, 2), ὁ (Heb. שִׁלֹחַ),
Siloam (v. DB, iii, 515 f.): Lk 13:4, Jo 9:7, 11.†

σιτευτός.as:
σιτευτός, -ή, -όν
(< σιτεύω, to feed, fatten), [in LXX: III Ki 4:23 (אָבַס), etc. ;]
fattened: Lk 15:23, 27, 30.†

σινιάζω.long: I sift, prove by trials, winnow.
σινιάζω.as:
*† σινιάζω
(< σίνιον, a sieve), = σήθω,
to sift, winnow: fig., Lk 22:31.†

σιτίον.as:
σιτίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of σῖτος), [in LXX: Pr 24:57 (30:22)(לֶחֶם) *;]
1.corn, grain: Ac 7:12 (but v. Bl., §9, 1).
2. Mostly in pl., σιτία, bread, food, provisions (LXX, l.c., Hdt., al.).†

Σινᾶ.sd: Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia
Σινᾶ.as:
Σινά
(-ᾶ, Rec.),
indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό
(Heb. סִינַי),
Sinai (Ex 19:11, al.): Ac 7:30, 38, Ga 4:24, 25.†

σιδηροῦς.as:
σιδήρεος, -α, -ον (-οῦς, -ᾶ -οῦν)
(< σίδηρος), [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]
of iron: Ac 12:10, Re 2:279:912:519:15.†

Σίλας.long: Silas, a pet-form of the name "Silvanus"; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.
Σίλας.as:
Σίλας, -α (acc to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; v. Dalman, Gr., 1575),
Silas (called also Σιλουανός, q.v.): Ac 15:22, 27, 32, 34, 4016:19, 25, 2917:4, 10, 14, 1518:5 †

Σιλᾶς.long: Silas, a pet-form of the name "Silvanus"; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.
Σιλᾶς.as:
Σίλας, -α (acc to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; v. Dalman, Gr., 1575),
Silas (called also Σιλουανός, q.v.): Ac 15:22, 27, 32, 34, 4016:19, 25, 2917:4, 10, 14, 1518:5 †

σιμικίνθιον.sd: a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron)
σιμικίνθιον.as:
*† σιμικίνθιον (also written σημι-), -ου, τό (Lat. semicinctium),
a work­man's apron: Ac 19:12.†

σικάριος.long: an assassin, murderer, bandit; one of the Sicarii.
σικάριος.sd: a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans)
σικάριος.as:
*† σικάριος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat.; < sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii),
a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Ac 21:38.†

σιγή.der: apparently from (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush);
σιγή.as:
** σιγή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: Wi 18:14, III Mac 3:23 * ;]
silence: Ac 21:40, Re 8:1.†

Σιλουανός.long: Silvanus, a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.
Σιλουανός.as:
Σιλουανός
(in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form freq. in π.), -οῦ, ὁ,
Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: II Co 1:19, I Th 1:1, II Th 1:1, I Pe 5:12.†

σιρικός.sd: hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric)
σιρικός.der: from (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured;
σιρικός.as:
* σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; v. Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν
(< οἱΣῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk),
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Re 18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†

σίδηρος.as:
σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]
iron: Re 18:12.†
